Solvers

class pygeox.solver.SolverNamespace(scene)[source]

Bases: object

analytical()[source]

Attempt to solve the constraint system symbolically (analytically).

Steps:

  • Substitute mapping constraints.

  • Separate equations and inequalities.

  • Solve equalities using SymPy.

  • Filter and validate solutions.

  • Return unique solution or multiple candidates.

Raises:

ValueError – If no solution or invalid solutions found.

Returns:

Solution mapping symbols to values.

Return type:

dict or list of dicts

get_objective_function(variables, equations, alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, strict_penalty=1.0, strict_tol=0.0001, use_numba=False)[source]

Build the objective function for numerical optimization from constraints.

Supports both pure Python and Numba-jitted versions.

Parameters:

  • variables – List of variables to optimize.

  • equations – List of (description, sympy expression) constraints.

  • alpha (float) – Weight for equality constraints.

  • beta (float) – Weight for inequality constraints.

  • strict_penalty (float) – Penalty for strict inequality violations.

  • strict_tol (float) – Tolerance for strict inequalities.

  • use_numba (bool) – If True, return a Numba-accelerated function.

Returns:

(objective function, variables, dictionary of sub-objectives)

Return type:

tuple

has_any_overlapping_points(threshold=0.0001)[source]
numerical(method='basinhoping', seed=None, alpha=1.0, beta=1.0, strict_penalty=1.0, strict_tol=0.0001, distance_penalty=1, min_dist=None, use_numba=True, save_param_history=False, verbose=True)[source]

Solve the constraint system numerically using global or local optimization.

Supports methods like basinhopping, L-BFGS-B, and dual_annealing.

Parameters:

  • method – Optimization method name.

  • seed – Random seed.

  • alpha – Penalty weights and tolerances.

  • beta – Penalty weights and tolerances.

  • strict_penalty – Penalty weights and tolerances.

  • strict_tol – Penalty weights and tolerances.

  • distance_penalty (float) – Weight for penalty avoiding degenerate configurations.

  • min_dist (float | None) – Minimum allowed distance between points.

  • use_numba (bool) – Use Numba-accelerated objective function.

  • save_param_history (bool) – Save parameter values during optimization.

  • verbose (bool) – Print detailed solver progress.

Returns:

Dictionary with all objects with scene and solved numerical values.

Return type:

dict

Raises:

ValueError – If optimization fails.

numerical_analysis(x=None, verbose=True)[source]

Evaluate and report the quality of a numerical solution.

Prints objective value, satisfaction of equality, inequality, strict, and not-equal constraints, and warns about overlapping points.

Parameters:

  • x – Optional solution vector to evaluate.

  • verbose – Whether to print detailed report.

Returns:

Analysis summary including objective and constraint values.

Return type:

dict

pick_solution(index=None, ind_var_values=None)[source]

Select and apply one solution among multiple symbolic solutions.

Parameters:

  • index (int) – Index of the solution to pick (random if None).

  • ind_var_values (dict) – Optional fixed values for independent variables.

Raises:

ValueError – If solution contains invalid values or fails inequalities.

simplify_constraints(max_linear=0)[source]

Simplify the constraint system by applying known variable mappings, removing trivial equalities, and optionally performing cheap linear eliminations.

This reduces the number of independent variables and constraints, aiding solver efficiency.

Parameters:

max_linear (int) – Maximum number of additional cheap linear eliminations to attempt.

Returns:

  • indep_vars (list[sympy.Symbol]): Independent variables after simplification.

  • reduced_eqs (list[sympy.Expr]): Simplified constraint expressions (lhs - rhs).

  • mapping (dict[sympy.Symbol, sympy.Expr]): Mapping from dependent to independent variables.

  • red_full_mapping (dict[sympy.Symbol, sympy.Expr]): Final mapping of variables to expressions.

Return type:

tuple
